title: Planarian head shapes may be attractors of a gap-junction-coupled bioelectric network

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Planarian head shapes may be attractors of a gap-junction-coupled bioelectric network

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The authors hypothesize that distinct planarian head shapes may be attractors in the state space of the bioelectric network formed by body cells coupled by gap junctions, that these attractors correspond to regions of morphospace in the evolutionary sense, and that octanol knocks the network's stochastic dynamics into one of several nearby attractors normally belonging to other flatworm species.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.7. A hypothesis: Physiological Network Attractors Underlie Regions of Anatomical Morphospace

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We hypothesize that distinct shape outcomes may be attractors in a state space describing distinct modes of the bioelectric network of planarian body cells connected by gap junctions (electrical synapses); in essence, these attractors correspond to regions of a morphospace as classically understood by evolutionary theory [151].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “3. Discussion › 3.7. A hypothesis: Physiological Network Attractors Underlie Regions of Anatomical Morphospace”. Scope: Planarian body-wide bioelectric networks (G. dorotocephala and related species)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-19: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.34

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Attractors have measurable dynamical signatures and perturbation predictions, so the hypothesis is testable in principle. The required trajectories are absent; discrete outcomes by themselves are insufficient evidence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Infer state-space dynamics from longitudinal cell-resolved voltage and connectivity data, test for reproducible basins predicting discrete head outcomes, and perturb states near inferred basin boundaries. Attractor-specific outcome switching would support the hypothesis.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Static morphology alone cannot establish dynamical attractors.

The source explicitly lacks cell-resolution spatiotemporal voltage and connectivity data.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.25
data adequacy: 0.05
data existence: 0.1
discriminating power: 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Multistability, return, and perturbation-induced switching are measurable signatures of attractors, so the hypothesis is testable in principle. The paper reports discrete shapes and later remodeling, and it does not provide the state trajectories that would separate attractors from other routes to a few head classes. Those recordings are still required.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate the voltage-and-shape state of regenerating animals and test for a small set of stable head shapes, return after small perturbations, and switching among those shapes after gap-junction block. A continuous cloud of shapes, or no return to discrete states, would refute an attractor account of the observed heads.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Discrete outcome classes can be produced by thresholds that are not attractors of a bioelectric network.

No public time series links network state to the evolutionary morphospace regions named in the hypothesis.
